title: T-2374: the Agency House's front aperture count, from its own picture
body:
## T-2374 — the Agency House's front aperture count, from its own picture

**One bounded visible increment of T-2374, not a completed image match.** The ticket
stays OPEN after this merges.

### What the picture shows, and what I did with it

The ticket's own source — the keyed panorama "Fort Dearborn and Chicago in 1831"
(`kinzie_1857_chicago_1831_panorama`, the verified public-domain Wentworth 1881
reproduction crediting Wau-Bun; local copy sha256 `624d8f1f…84c3f`) — draws the
Agency House's front gable with **THREE dark marks**: TWO upright ones standing on
the ground line, and ONE small one high on the face. I opened the full-resolution
original and read that subject directly, at 14× and against a per-pixel threshold
map of the gable face; both readings agree on the count and on the arrangement.

The model had **one centred door and no upper mark**. It could not have had anything
else: `log_dwelling`'s compound path states ONE opening per room (`front_opening`:
a door or a window on the middle of that room's wall), so this front was not sayable
in data at all. Splitting the centre room to get a second opening would change the
roof and the walls the rest of the record states, and is not acceptable.

### The change

A narrowly opt-in `compound_apertures` set on the ordinary five-room compound path,
local to `log_dwelling.py` / `log_dwelling_params.py` plus the target record.

- Each entry is `(room, face, zone, kind, u0, u1, z0, z1)`. `zone` is `wall` (in the
  log wall, below the eave) or `gable` (on the closed gable that room's roof carries,
  placed with the archetype's existing `GABLE_FACE_OUT` convention, never buried in
  the roof or floating in front of it).
- **A stated set OVERRIDES its room's singular `front_opening`**, so the old centre
  door does not survive as a phantom among the new marks — not in the mesh, and not
  in the front-wall reading that `facade_openings`, `generate_business_signboards`
  and `generate_entrances` all share. The builder and the readers use the **same
  returned rectangles**.
- `kind` is deliberately thin. `aperture` claims a hole and nothing else: a sawn
  casing with its reveal running back to a dark face, no sash, glass, leaf, shutter
  or closure. `aperture` joins `facade_openings.HOLE_KINDS` (a board must clear it,
  two of them may not run together) and is **not** an entrance kind.
- At most **one** aperture in a set may be a `door`, which is a stated reconstruction
  of a way in and never a reading of a picture.
- Validation is strict and refuses, with one self-test case per rule: an unstated
  room, a boolean index, a face that is not outward, an unsupported face/zone/kind,
  a non-finite or boolean coordinate, a negative extent, a wall aperture past its
  room's corner or into the wall head, a gable aperture below the eave or through or
  off its own rake, a way in that does not reach the ground or sits up in the gable,
  two ways in, apertures that overlap or leave no wall between them, an empty set,
  more than six, a missing key, a set on the bounded elbow, and a set on a record
  with no stated rooms. **No existing validator was broadened or weakened.**

**Cobweb's set** (all coordinates reconstructed, see below): two apertures on the
centre room's own front wall at `u 4.26–5.16` and `6.22–7.12`, both in the 0.02–1.95 m
band this archetype already gives a log cabin's door; one 0.70 × 0.80 m light on the
centre gable at `u 5.57–6.27`, `z 2.74–3.54`, clear of that roof's rake.

### Provenance — what is read and what is ours

**Read:** the count, that the lower pair stand on the ground, and roughly where the
three fall along the face (the lower pair in the face's left and middle leaving the
right-hand stretch blank; the upper mark a little left of the apex). The face is
drawn slightly oblique, which compresses its right-hand side, so even the arrangement
is read with that caution.

**Reconstructed:** every coordinate. The marks are a few pixels across a thirty-pixel
gable in a retrospective engraving whose proportions are not this model's, so no
fraction is carried across as a measurement — the set-out comes from this record's
own 5 m centre wall and its own rake. So is the recess section, and so is the entry
role: the picture does not say which mark was a door or that either was. The
right-hand one is built as one because it stands where the previous centre door stood,
so the town's **one grounded entrance on that front stays one entrance** (it moves
0.17 m and narrows to 0.90 m as the apron re-derives onto it).

No glazing, closure, interior, attic room, white paint or historic function is
claimed. The engraving's white paper is not evidence of paint. `L-cobweb-apertures-2374`
records all of it; `docs/STATUS.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md` carry the honest state.

### Native build — actually run, actually measured

Pinned Blender **4.5.3** on **Ubuntu 26.04.1**, tarball sha256 verified against
`generators/blender.pin` before use. All **82** log_dwelling masters regenerated in
four bounded foreground batches (2.7 s, 2.8 s, 2.7 s, 2.7 s), then
`stale_derivatives.py` → `web_derivatives.sh --only` (18.3 s), `compile_scene.py --all`,
`generate_entrances.py`, `publish.sh`.

**81 of the 82 masters came out byte-identical.** That is the measurement that the
new option is genuinely absent/default-off for every other record, including the
accepted Eliza school, Wolf elbow, Miller and Carpenter defaults.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| MASTER | `af1f33c0f5d75fc8c40e6cbb589adfd7d29d551572c2775e236bb260f6ee561f` (139,824 B) | `4f42207be5fcb2391fda58672ce8442b02aba9510f3096db8c2934b695fe7bea` (139,248 B) |
| WEB | `49cfcb869c0a39bd936c2c22428179538c37c5a380b9f27c53fab019719b8dcd` (31,804 B) | `1699d7aa1c4b0abb6229bd4cbfaed95013f3ede9323f4945396583fd14b26e23` (30,304 B) |

No other archetype family, structure version or foreign registry row is touched;
the merged Sauganash, Pruyne/Kimball and Dearborn-bridge rows on current `dev` are
preserved. No shared `common/openings.py`, `logwork.py`, `mesh.py`, `emit.py`,
`materials.py`, generic schema or recipe scheme was edited.

### Verification

- `tools/check.sh --part 1/4 … 4/4`, each a bounded foreground call, **all four
  green** — 1,150 steps, none red (503 s / 420 s / 318 s / 391 s). Run **before** the
  first source commit. No gate step stood on a banked reading: numpy, scipy, Pillow,
  pyproj, jsonschema, openpyxl and pypdf are all installed here and the only
  "not installed" lines in the transcript are the tagged self-test proving that
  warning fires.
- `tools/preflight.sh`'s other two questions, which `check.sh` cannot ask:
  `check-changelog-entry.mjs` against the merge base (entry present) and
  `resolve_id_collisions.mjs --check` (not applicable — tickets are their own repo).
- `tools/test_log_compound_apertures.py` — 44 checks, all green, added to the gate
  as one `step` and one `selftest`; its row added to `tools/step_isolation.json`
  (measured, writes nothing in-tree).
- Smoke parts and both-viewport application QA: see the comment below.

### What this does NOT settle

The panorama's camera remains **UNSOLVED** and is not enrolled in
`data/reference_views/`; no `matches` verdict, grade upgrade or completion is
claimed. The compound's overall width, the wing and sub-roof silhouettes, the roof
junctions and valleys, the text-attested partial clapboarding "part way up", and the
building's finish and tone are all unchanged and still differ from the picture. The
source is retrospective 1831 context printed in 1881, not proof of the building as it
stood on 1835-07-01. **T-2374's image gate stays open** and the ticket is released
back to the queue after this lands, with the remaining differences recorded. No new
photo follow-up ticket, no split, no `done --anyway`.
